problem: Domain shift causes deep models to fail when visual features don't transfer across datasets.
approach: Leverage reasoning chains from multimodal LLMs to create robust predictions under domain shift using Multi-Task Cross-Training and Self-Aligned Reasoning Regularization.
contribution: RD-MLDG framework achieves improved robustness on DomainBed datasets by combining direct classification with reasoning supervision.

problem: Neural combinatorial optimization treats solutions as monolithic references, missing fine-grained local decision patterns.
approach: Apply masked generation as self-supervised learning on solutions, masking portions and training models to recover missing content.
contribution: MaskCO turns single (instance, solution) pairs into hundreds of training examples and enables local-search-like refinement during inference.

problem: Deep generative models face a quality-generalization tradeoff where high sample quality leads to memorization.
approach: Regularize probability paths with geometry-aware noise whose covariance captures local data manifold structure.
contribution: CDC-FM consistently improves quality-generalization tradeoff across diverse datasets and architectures, with significant gains in data-scarce and non-uniform regimes.

problem: Diffusion Transformer acceleration via caching suffers from computational error that varies unpredictably during denoising.
approach: Formulate dynamic programming algorithm with cumulative error approximation to optimize caching strategy for fidelity minimization.
contribution: CEM plugin significantly improves generation fidelity of existing acceleration models across nine generation models and three tasks.

problem: Vision-Language Models suffer catastrophic forgetting when sequentially fine-tuned on multiple tasks.
approach: Use model fusion to maintain unified model with task triggers and prototype sets, iteratively decoupling and unifying task experts.
contribution: ConDU achieves up to 2% improvement in average performance while enhancing zero-shot capabilities on MTIL benchmark.

problem: World models for autonomous driving waste computation on static regions and lack deep interaction with trajectories.
approach: Extract dynamic objects via temporal residuals, predict future spatial distribution, and refine trajectories with future-guided interaction.
contribution: TR-World achieves state-of-the-art planning performance on nuScenes and NAVSIM datasets.

problem: Long-story generation struggles with semantic consistency across many frames when using fixed reference images.
approach: Propose iterative paradigm that refines each generated image using all previous reference images with global reference cross-attention module.
contribution: Story-Iter achieves state-of-the-art performance in long-story visualization up to 100 frames with improved semantic consistency.

problem: Reference-based super-resolution datasets focus on limited scene types, missing complex plant textures and fine details.
approach: Construct large-scale plant dataset with selective key-region matching and texture-guided diffusion for matching and refinement.
contribution: PlantRSR dataset comprises 16,585 HR-Ref pairs; proposed method significantly improves SOTA on plant imagery.

problem: Existing methods for dynamic text-attributed graphs neglect recent-global temporal semantics and face efficiency issues with LLMs.
approach: Combine node-centric implicit reasoning with sliding window and explicit reasoning via tailored prompts to capture temporal and global semantics.
contribution: DyGRASP achieves up to 34% improvement in Hit@10 for destination node retrieval on dynamic graph benchmarks.

problem: End-to-end backpropagation requires storing activations throughout all layers, creating memory bottlenecks for model scalability.
approach: Convert residual updates to denoising process updates where each block learns independently via score matching objective.
contribution: DiffusionBlocks enables block-wise training matching end-to-end performance while reducing memory proportional to block count.

problem: Discrete, unordered graph structures are difficult for traditional generative models to handle effectively.
approach: Iterate refinements over continuous distribution parameters using Bayesian Sample Inference, modeling graphs via SDE.
contribution: GraphBSI achieves state-of-the-art performance on molecular and synthetic graph generation benchmarks.

problem: Multi-agent systems with LLMs suffer from excessive token consumption and failures from misinformation.
approach: Introduce SupervisorAgent lightweight framework with LLM-free context filter to intervene at critical junctures for error correction.
contribution: SupervisorAgent reduces token consumption by average 29.68% without compromising success rate on GAIA benchmark.

problem: Multi-Resolution Hash Encoding lacks rigorous understanding of spatial behavior, leading to heuristic hyperparameter selection.
approach: Analyze encoding via Point Spread Function to characterize spatial resolution and fidelity; apply rotations to mitigate anisotropy.
contribution: R-MHE mitigates grid-induced anisotropy while maintaining efficiency and parameter count of original approach.

problem: Fixed-architecture designs for dynamic graphs under distribution shifts become suboptimal as shifts evolve over time.
approach: Propose adaptive mixture of architecture experts with spatio-temporal distribution detector and prototype-guided routing.
contribution: AdaMix adaptively routes experts to varying distribution shifts and learns spatio-temporal invariant patterns.

problem: LoRA and similar parameter-efficient fine-tuning methods can exacerbate Catastrophic Inheritance of biases from pretraining.
approach: Incorporate consistency, diversity, and SVD regularizers to preserve knowledge, enforce representation richness, and stabilize updates.
contribution: BA-LoRA outperforms LoRA variants in performance, stability, and bias mitigation across NLU and NLG tasks.

problem: RL training of large reasoning models requires long rollouts with full-cache backpropagation, consuming excessive memory.
approach: Progressively encode intermediate reasoning into compact representations for fixed-size cache inference.
contribution: Progressive Thought Encoding achieves +19.3% improvement over LoRA and +29.9% over baseline on mathematical benchmarks.

problem: LLM outputs could evade monitoring through steganography to hide harmful information.
approach: Evaluate steganographic capabilities of frontier LLMs via encoded message passing and encoded reasoning tasks.
contribution: Current models show nascent steganographic capabilities but cannot reliably hide reasoning under standard affordances.

problem: Existing RL methods for code generation rely on outcome rewards without optimizing verification or leveraging realistic feedback.
approach: Structure long-horizon reasoning as iterative generation-verification turns with turn-level credit assignment and self-constructed tests.
contribution: ReVeal enables code evolution for 20+ turns despite training on three, significantly improving Pass@k on LiveCodeBench.

problem: Fine-tuning on narrowly harmful datasets can cause emergent misalignment, giving evil responses across unrelated settings.
approach: Use linear representation analysis to compare general misalignment solution with narrow task solution.
contribution: General misalignment is more stable, efficient, and robust than narrow solution, providing basis for monitoring and mitigation.

problem: Poisoned sample detection effectiveness degrades significantly under weak backdoor attacks.
approach: Amplify backdoor effect through Sharpness-Aware Minimization training to enhance detection features.
contribution: SAM-enhanced PSD achieves average TPR gain of +34.3% over conventional methods under both strong and weak attacks.

problem: Designing effective ambiguity sets for DRO requires balancing consistency with nominal distribution and diversity.
approach: Use generative models to create ambiguity sets capturing adversarial distributions while maintaining consistency.
contribution: GAS-DRO with diffusion model demonstrates superior out-of-distribution generalization in ML tasks.

problem: NL2SQL requires expensive test-time scaling with large private models; small public models lack effective decomposition.
approach: Use AST-guided search for decomposition synthesis and margin-aware RL for fine-grained preference optimization.
contribution: LearNAT achieves GPT-4 comparable results with 7B model, enabling openness and efficiency.

problem: Extracting syntax from neural language models via probing faces limitations in complexity and requires additional training.
approach: Estimate mutual information and directly extract dependency trees from attention scores without additional network training.
contribution: Method probes complex dependency trees transparently with simpler models than previous approaches.

problem: Feature sensitivity examples in tree ensembles often lie far from training distribution, limiting interpretability.
approach: Constrain sensitive examples to remain close to dataset using MILP and SMT encodings for realistic evidence.
contribution: Data-aware framework scales to ensembles with up to 800 trees, achieving substantial improvements over SOTA.

problem: Internal mechanisms by which LLMs perform translation remain incompletely understood.
approach: Identify token alignment heads responsible for source-to-target language mapping via systematic investigation.
contribution: Token alignment heads are universal, sparse, consistent, causal for translation, and show specific functionality.

problem: Scaling laws for in-context learning depend on multiple resources; their interplay with architecture is unclear.
approach: Analyze in-context learning of linear regression in deep linear self-attention models across width, depth, context length.
contribution: Depth aids ICL only with limited context in isotropic/fixed settings, but significantly helps with changing covariances.

problem: Scaling laws focus on asymptotic end-of-training behavior, missing the full training dynamics.
approach: Analyze entire training dynamics to derive dynamical scaling laws governing performance evolution with norm-based complexity.
contribution: Novel dynamical scaling laws recover well-known asymptotic scaling and hold across CNNs, ResNets, and Vision Transformers.

problem: Large multimodal models struggle with tightly interleaved image-text generation due to limited dataset quality and scale.
approach: Create InterSyn dataset with 1.8M samples using SEIR for quality refinement and SynJudge for comprehensive evaluation.
contribution: 25K-50K samples yield substantial improvements; scaling to 200K brings further gains in content and cross-modal synergy.

problem: No benchmark evaluates whether AI agents can implement experiments from papers with varied amounts of code available.
approach: Create AutoExperiment benchmark with progressive code masking ranging from partial reproduction to full replication.
contribution: Performance degrades rapidly as difficulty increases; interactive debugging agents outperform fixed harnesses.

problem: Measuring and regularizing memorization in neural networks requires direct empirical methods beyond theoretical Rademacher complexity.
approach: Augment training with auxiliary random labels predicted by RLP-heads attached at arbitrary depths to track memorization.
contribution: RLP-head performance provides direct memorization measure; proposed regularization reduces memorization with variable generalization effects.

problem: Effect of scaled post-training on pretrained knowledge remains poorly understood beyond task-level metrics.
approach: Use sample-wise paradigm counting 1->0 and 0->1 transitions to quantify forgetting and backward transfer.
contribution: Framework reveals domain-continual pretraining induces moderate forgetting, while RL/SFT show substantial backward transfer.

problem: Existing vertical federated learning imposes restrictive assumptions on data alignment and labeling scenarios.
approach: Reinterpret alignment gaps as missing data problems; use deep latent variable models for flexible training and inference.
contribution: Unified framework handles arbitrary alignment, unlabeled data, and multi-party collaboration, outperforming baselines in 160/168 configurations.

problem: KV cache memory is quadratic bottleneck in long-horizon LLM inference despite various optimization attempts.
approach: Learn token retention importance at creation time via lightweight gate predicting scalar retention scores that decay over time.
contribution: TRIM-KV outperforms baselines especially in low-memory regimes and can surpass full-cache models via regularization.

problem: Gradient ascent unlearning causes probability mass to redistribute to semantically related high-likelihood rephrasings (squeezing effect).
approach: Bootstrap unlearning framework linking squeezing effect to model beliefs by jointly suppressing targets and high-confidence generations.
contribution: BS-T and BS-S achieve more thorough forgetting while preserving utility better than existing unlearning methods.

problem: Standard pullback approach for diffusion latent spaces forces geodesics to decode as straight segments, ignoring data geometry.
approach: Use stochastic decoder via reverse SDE with information geometric treatment; introduce latent spacetime indexing denoising distributions.
contribution: Establishes nontrivial geometric structure via exponential family distributions; enables simulation-free geodesic computation.

problem: CNNs lack global context without deep architectures; ViTs lack spatial inductive bias and depend on positional encodings.
approach: Use continuous spectral parameterization with orientation-selective components defining smooth frequency domain responses.
contribution: SONIC shows improved robustness to geometric transformations and matches architectures with order of magnitude fewer parameters.

problem: Sparse training of SNNs fails to achieve ultra-sparse structures without significant performance loss.
approach: Use sparse spike correlated topological initialization, sparse spike weight initialization, hybrid link removal, and link prediction.
contribution: CH-SNN achieves high structural sparsity while maintaining performance comparable to fully connected networks.

problem: Vision-Language-Action models rely on expert demonstrations and cannot learn from failures via RL on real robots due to high sample complexity.
approach: Use pixel-based world models with on-policy GRPO for self-improving VLA policy without real robot interaction.
contribution: WMPO achieves stronger overall performance, emergent self-correction, and robust generalization with improved sample efficiency.

problem: Modern high-dimensional text representations lack interpretable geometric properties like early word embeddings.
approach: Represent semantic-syntactic transformations as consistent rotational operations in embedding space using RISE.
contribution: RISE consistently maps discourse-level transformations across languages and models, supporting Linear Representation Hypothesis.

problem: Standard MoE routing mechanisms overlook time-varying interaction dynamics between modalities.
approach: Guide MoE routing using quantified temporal multimodal interaction; router learns to dispatch based on interaction nature.
contribution: Framework improves performance and interpretability of MoE-based models on multimodal benchmarks.
